audio_captions: A man speaks, "Joining me now from Salt Lake City, Utah, Republican Congresswoman Mia Love. Congresswoman, I want to start with a comment this week by one of your colleagues in the house, Congresswoman Barbara Comstock. Here she is." This is followed by a short musical sting.

A woman speaks, "young staffer, as a young woman, went there and was greeted with a member in a towel. It was a male, who then invited her in. Um, at that point, he decided to expose himself. She left and then she quit her job." The sound of papers rustling is also heard.
A man asks, "Congresswoman, how serious a problem is there with sexual harassment in Congress? And if you can tell us, have you or any of your staffers been a victim?" A woman responds, "Well, I..."

A person speaks, "I can tell you this has been going on for a very long time. And I'm glad that people are speaking out about it. I'm, you know, it's important to speak out about it nationally and also locally and in our homes. I have two girls that I'm raising, one going off to college and it's important that we have uh we're comfortable having uncomfortable conversations so that we can uh protect our our young women and protect women in the in the workspace." Another person then says, "Let's talk about".

A man speaks, "about your workspace because it turns out that Congress has protected itself with a much more challenging, much more cumbersome process than we see in the private sector. I want to put this up. I think people will be surprised. A victim who claims sexual harassment in Congress must wait three months to file a complaint. First, submit to 30 days of counseling and another 30 days of mediation, then wait another 30 days to seek a hearing. And Congresswoman, it gets even worse than that because if there is a settlement, it's paid for by taxpayers, not by the individual member of Congress. Is this another case of the old boys clubby network on Capitol Hill protecting itself?" A woman then begins to speak, "Well, it's the only"

A woman speaks, "woman in the Utah delegation, I I have a little bit of a problem with that. We, our office has made sure that they have taken all of the anti-sexual harassment training and I led out on that, taking it myself. Um, I think we need some leadership. We need people that are out there that are talking about this and talking about how uh situations like this, behavior like this is absolutely inappropriate. But I'd also like to say one more thing. I think it's important that we, especially the things that are going on out there, that this is not being politicized, it's not being used for personal gain, because we normalize the situation if that if and when that happens. We have to make sure that the we're not going out there doing anything that is going to further victimize people who have actually been hurt and who've been humiliated by sexual harassment and and and sexual misconduct." This is followed by a man speaking, "Well, let me..."
A person speaks, "ask you about two specific cases. Do you believe..." followed by a prolonged buzzing sound.
A man speaks, "that Judge Roy Moore, the candidate in the special Senate election in Alabama, should step aside."
A male speaker says, "from that race to let a write-in candidate try to hold the seat for Republicans."
A man asks, "and what do you think should happen to Senator Al Franken after the allegations against him this week?" Another voice begins to speak.

A woman speaks, "calling them all on the carpet. I think that all of them should take responsibility for their behavior. This is, you know, when you think about Al Franken, you think about Judge Moore, you think about all of these situations that are out there. They're all different, and they all deserve due process, and the people need to be able to have time to to talk about it and process it. We certainly aren't going to be able to do that today in seven minutes on a Sunday show, but I think it's important that we end up talking about it, getting comfortable having uncomfortable conversations and saying that this type of behavior is unacceptable." A man responds, "Well, let me ask you about one other person."

A man speaks in a clear, articulate voice, "and whether or not he should be held accountable. And that is President Trump, who has had very little to say about the Judge Roy Moore case, but when it comes to Al Franken and that picture, he weighed in on that, the picture of Franken appearing to grope his accuser. Uh, the president sent out this tweet, 'The Al Franken-stein picture is really bad, speaks a thousand words. Where do his hands go in pictures two, three, four, five, and six while she sleeps?' On the other hand, when reporters noted that President Trump faces his own allegations from a bunch of women about him allegedly groping them, here's what his spokeswoman said."
A woman speaks in a clear, direct voice: "I think in one case specifically, uh, Senator Franken has admitted wrongdoing and the president hasn't. I think that's a very clear distinction."
A man speaks, "Congresswoman, does that satisfy you, the fact that President Trump has denied the allegations?"

A woman speaks, "Well, again, all of these situations are completely different. I think people need to take responsibility for their actions, not just in the future, but also in the past. And we can't, it's absolutely, I'm not qualified nor is it appropriate for us to process, prosecute, judge and sentence, um, in in the seven minutes that we have here. But I think it is important that we all speak out and we prevent these things from happening. This is about looking towards the future and making sure that women are empowered and no longer victimized. That people, if they are experiencing situations in the office that makes them uncomfortable, that they feel empowered, that they can actually speak out and stop the behavior." This is followed by a man speaking, "Congresswoman..."
A male voice says, "Thank you. Thanks for your time." A female voice responds, "Thank you." A musical tone then plays.

A man speaks, "Well, changes have been made to the Marine unit's protocols including visits from management several times a week." A musical news jingle plays as an announcer says, "And now from WMAR 2 News, Maryland's most accurate forecast." Another man speaks, "Well, shaping up once again to be a hot and humid day on Thursday, but scattered strong storms look to put an end to that humidity pretty quickly as we get towards the afternoon and evening hours, packing a punch with damaging gusty winds as well as the concern for flash flooding. A gentle piano melody plays.

The rogue regime of North Korea also has been doubling down on its own threats, saying absolute force is the only way to deal with the US. Former Vice Chief of Staff of the US Army and Fox News contributor, he is retired four-star General Jack Keane joins me now. Good to see you, General."

Do you really think the North Koreans will fire off missiles in the waters near Guam?" Another man begins to reply, "Well, it doesn't make much sense to me that they would take..."

A man with a serious voice speaks, "that kind of provocation because clearly the United States will respond militarily. You know, what what the North Koreans, their calculation is sound, and this is what I mean. They they believe that the only way to stop the United States from taking down the regime in North Korea is not and not just to have nuclear weapons pointed at the South, is what they've been doing for 10 years. It's to hold the American people at risk. That's their calculation. And they also believe we would accept that reality as we have accepted nuclear weapons in North Korea. So, if you if you believe that, that that's their calculation, and I absolutely do believe that, then what they're truly trying to prevent is the end of their regime, which means they're not going to fire weapons at Guam, which would require."

A man speaks, "an incredible response by the United States because Guam is an ally. We have military bases there. We have hundreds of thousands of American citizens there. We're not going to tolerate something something like that. So, clearly, I I don't think they would do it, frankly. I think it's more saber-rattling than anything else and face-saving going on within the North Korea elite that clearly understand what's happening here." A woman asks, "If they did shoot missiles near Guam, what would the US response be?" The man replies, "Well, I think the United States, I'm not even convinced they would let them shoot the missiles to begin with. Uh, so that's another calculation that our military certainly has the capability to deal with. They may take those missiles out before they're before they're launched. Why would we permit them to launch those missiles and endanger the lives of people that are there? So that's option one. Option two, clearly, once launched, we would shoot them down and there would be a military response. And the scale of which is is the president's decision, certainly." Another woman says, "You know, General, the, you know, North Korea is threatening the entire region, Japan, uh, China's under threat, South Korea."

A female speaker says, "...and he's brutalized his own people. That's well-documented. President Trump is getting criticized for his rhetoric. Democrats Diane Feinstein and Charles Schumer doesn't like it, John McCain doesn't like it. They're saying this is reckless rhetoric. What do you say?" This is followed by the sound of an object being placed on a hard surface. A male speaker then says, "Well, I don't think I would have chosen quite those words, Mike."

A person speaks, "self, but he's the president, he chose them. Here's what I think the words are about. The words are simply about that he wants China and the North Korean leadership to clearly understand that the policy of appeasement and accommodation that his predecessor exercised with North Korea, with Iran, with with Syria is over. And we will not tolerate the the path that they are on and endanger the American people. That's why the strong language exists. Whether we whether he could have used different language, I think is put past the point. That's the message he wants to get to them. It's reinforced by Secretary of State Tillerson and reinforced by Secretary of Defense Mattis. And I clearly, we are on the same page here in the United States from the National Security team from the from the Commander-in-Chief down, that we are not, we are not going to tolerate military provocation by by North Korea against any of the United States interests." Another speaker begins to say, "You know, John F Kennedy".

A woman speaks, "his real fear during the Cuban missile crisis was an accidental nuclear war due to miscommunication and freak occurrences beyond the U.S.'s control. Here's the president commenting on past presidents. Roll tape." This is followed by a whooshing sound. A man then says, "They've been negotiating now for 25 years. Look at Clinton. He folded on the negotiations. He was weak and ineffective. You look what happened with Bush, you look what happened with Obama. Obama, he didn't even want to talk about it. But I talk. It's about time. Somebody has to do it." A woman asks, "What are your thoughts here, General?" A man replies, "No, I I think he's..."

A man speaks, "absolutely right. We we've had 25 years of coddling the North Koreans because of their bellicose language, because of their intensity. And now, what we have is a president that one is not going to tolerate it and he he is trying to communicate and get inside their head that I'm serious here." A woman then asks, "Is there a chance for any miscommunication, is there a chance for any miscommunication or something that happens beyond the US's control as this heated rhetoric..."
A female voice asks, "continues?" A man with a deep voice replies, "Well surely there is always that possibility, but when you go back to the prelude..."

A person speaks, "of the North Koreans themselves and why do they want nuclear weapons? And why do they want ICBMs? It's to preserve the regime. If they're going to take military action that would do guarantee the destruction of the regime, that makes no sense. Now, would they do that? I doubt it, seriously, because I don't... while the language coming out of North Korea is bombastic, it's bellicose, etc. their strategy is very rational from their national interest perspective." Another person begins to speak, "You know, the President also..."

A woman says, "responding to a question about a possible preemptive strike on North Korea. Let's take a listen." A swoosh sound is heard. Amidst the sound of a noisy crowd, a man asks, "Mr. President, if one of the options you consider a preemptive strike..." Another man replies, "We don't talk about that. I never do. I'm not like the other administration that would say we're going into Mosul in four months. I don't talk about it. We'll see what happens." The woman speaks again, "We'll see what happens. So to your point, sir, is North Korea's nuclear weapons program a negotiating tool, a way to inflate its own importance? So what does North Korea want? Does it want more diplomatic recognition, economic concessions? What does it want?" A man begins to respond, "Well, first of all, step number one, it's he wants that real military capability to possess..."

A man speaks, "...his regime. Number two, he wants to separate the United States from South Korea, and China plays at this as well so that eventually the US troops go home from South Korea. And number three, North Korea and China would clearly like to unite that peninsula, not under the rule of South Korea, but under the rule of North Korea. Now, that is a, that is a stretch to be sure, but nonetheless, those are their goals."

A woman speaks, saying, "both I know you were just in the Middle East as part of a congressional delegation. In fact, you just got back hours ago. So thank you for being here. You had a chance to visit Syrian refugee camps. Congressman Issa, I want to ask you the impact that had on you and how you connect that experience to San Diego."

A man speaks: "Well, both Juan and I have been to camps before, but this was the first time we were there together, particularly the the Lebanese camp. And uh obviously with millions of of Syrian refugees in the region, looking at it as more than just the local issue of how many can we take here in San Diego, uh what do we do for them? And I and I think that's where we gained a lot of insight into how far a dollar goes, what the employment is, what what the the goals are. And and Juan and I both listened to refugees talking about their desire to get back to their country and what are we, what is America going to do to make it safe for them to go home?" Another man begins to speak, "And congressman..."

A man speaks, "Vargas, this one's for you. What is your position on the recent U.S. action there, both the strikes in Syria and then what the military's calling the mother of all bombs that was dropped there in Afghanistan?" Another man begins to speak, "Well, I..."

A man speaks, "I think the president should come back to us and we should authorize the use of force again or not. I mean, we it does seem that we're escalating time and time again without them coming back and having the American people through the Congress decide if we're going too far now. A lot of these decisions are being made now militarily. And you know, that is the appropriate way I think to make it once you make a decision that this is where you want to go. Now, the MOAB, a lot of Americans are not familiar with it. The reality is that we in Congress have known about this for a long time. We knew that they were positioned for it, we knew they could be used at any time. They hadn't been used until now, and I think it is an escalation. But I do think that the president should come back to the Congress and ask us for the authorization, especially when he starts to do more and more things in Syria because I think that's outside of the authorization he got in 2001-2003." This is followed by a woman speaking, "Okay, and we were talking about MOAB of course, which was targeted..."

A woman speaks: "ISIS network of tunnels in Afghanistan. You were in Egypt not too far from the ISIS bombings at those Christian churches. Can you talk a little bit about what was happening while you were there and and again the the feeling about our fight against ISIS?" A man begins to reply, "Well, you know, we we actually went from."
A male voice speaks, "Egypt or from Cairo that morning out to the Sinai. So we were going away as it looked from what we thought was a safe area out to the forward operating base in the..."
A man speaks, "Sinai. And to be candid, more or less that day, we were meeting with some of the more than 500 soldiers that had been out there since the peace accords."
A man speaks, "in the late 70s, American soldiers. Uh, but we were also uh, to be candid, Ron was giving me communion for Palm Sunday."
A man speaks, "Uh, we were with the people who were there practicing their faith on one of our holiest days. Uh, but it was quite a shock that..."

A man speaks, "not one but two very vicious attacks that occurred against Catholics, against Copts there. And this is one of the challenges that the Egyptian President Sisi is facing is making sure that the remnants of the Muslim Brotherhood is not operating and at the same time dealing with multiple ISIS cells as they're now known." A second man then says, "And I've".

What are the next plans with with that in regards to that?" Another person responds, "Well, interestingly, Daryl and I are actually going to be there a little bit later."
A man speaks, "the matter is the system in Tijuana is is decrepit and falling apart. And so there's a long-term fix and that is they have to upgrade their s".
A male voice speaks, "your system, but that's going to take a long time and and certainly they don't have the..."
A person says, "do it right now. We have to".
A male voice speaks, "look at what are some of the interim things that we can do to help that out. So, we're actually out".
A man speaks, "...today with a lot of federal officials trying to figure that out. And I appreciate, of course..."
A male voice says, "the help from Daryl," followed by a low-pitched, prolonged buzzing sound.

A man says, "and they're a lot longer, knows the administration, this administration in particular, a lot better than I do. So, you know, I think it'll be help for both of us down there trying to figure this thing out." A woman then says, "We're almost".

A woman speaks, "time. Congressman Issa, last time you were here we talked about health care. You know what's happened since then. What what do we do now going forward?" A man then says, "Well, uh sometimes you deal with what's in front of you. Uh mapping the flows of sewage in through the Tijuana River is what we were doing this morning. Uh at some point we're obviously going to have to address some of the challenges in the Affordable Care Act and then go on on what I hope is a bipartisan basis to address the cost drivers. Uh the fact is the cost of health care is what's driving the increases that Americans are seeing and uh"
A man speaks, "you can't insure your way out of something cheaply if what it is is expensive. And and that's our challenge and uh is to quit the partisan behavior."
A person speaks, "and start looking."

A second male speaker says, "And John, a woman who was in that front seat told you this all started with a late-night food run." A low, rhythmic electronic tune plays in the background.

A man speaks, "And Stephen, Stephanie, this all involves an MCSO deputy's official truck, but he wasn't on scene, wasn't part of this. A male voice speaks, stating, "where a first-grade student from Fremont Elementary School."
A man says, "...has been hit by a car." A woman then says, "News specialist Andrew Adams has been on the scene since shortly after it happened and he joins us live now. Andrew?" A click is heard.

A male speaker says, "and you were only standing a couple hundred yards away from the school. That far lane, that southbound lane is where the accident happened just a little bit earlier on. Seven-year-old boy who was hit. Chopper 5." This is accompanied by the sound of helicopter rotor blades whirring.
A man speaks, "captured aerials of the accident scene a little bit earlier. Large response from Unified Police and Unified."
A male voice says, "Detectives say it appears the boy simply darted into the road and was hit by a southbound..."
A voice says, "three."

A male voice speaks, "from the witnesses that that we've talked to so far, they say, yeah, the the vehicle, the Dodge Durango was doing what they were supposed to be doing, and there was really nothing that the car could do." This is accompanied by the sound of background traffic.
A male voice speaks, "Investigators say there were no signs of impairment on the part of the driver. It's..."
A male voice speaks clearly, "unclear why the boy ran out in the road where he did. School was just getting out when this happened."
A man speaks, "and crossing guards were at work down the street. Now the boy was initially".

A male speaker states, "listed in critical condition, but since that time, just in about the past 20 minutes or so, we have an update. Sounds like fair condition with broken bones. Certainly an upgrade. For now, back to you."
A man speaks, "Yeah, hoping for the best here. All right, Andrew Adams live for us tonight. Andrew, thank you." A woman begins to speak, "Well, we've had".

A woman speaks, "...money on braces or Invisalign. I've actually done it three times, once as a teenager, twice as an adult. And the reason why is because my retainers probably weren't up to par. A man responds, "Um, it's not quite the best thing to do. It's common, it's something we run into all the time, but really there's a much better option out there for you. The woman responds, "No big tray, no goo, no choking. I'm in." Following this, there are a few light beeping sounds. The man says, "All right, so we're going to put you up here. That's it. A female voice says, "I mean, he's already a dentist, he's graduated."

A person speaks, "the highest and newest technology, like the 3D scanner today."

A person speaks, "...who is working to become a specialist, but are also overseen by mentoring faculty who are board certified and have been in practice."

Seven of those victims have been discharged from the hospital. 28-year-old Brenton Tarrant has been arrested and charged with murder. Police say it took 36 minutes from the first attack to the suspect's arrest. Eyewitnesses describe the chaotic scene. And everybody just run to the back doors.

A man speaks, "This attack has been condemned by world leaders, President..."
A male voice says, "says he spoke with the Prime Minister of Israel."

A woman speaks, "after 49 people were murdered at two mosques in New Zealand."

A male voice speaks, "it's felt that this morning they saw the patrols going around the school in the parking lot while they were learning in their classroom."

A female speaker says, "leaders worldwide condemning the terror attack." A male speaker then says, "These sacred places of worship were turned into scenes of evil killing. You've all been seeing what went on. It's a horrible, horrible thing." This is accompanied by the sound of camera shutters.
A person speaks, saying, "and the anti-Muslim ideology behind it."
A man speaks, "Islamophobia and hate that has been perpetrated by political leaders, by ideologues, by people who want to run for public office, by..."
A man speaks, "people who won public office on the backs of immigrants."
A man speaks in a calm, clear voice, "everyone to know about the Muslim community in the United States. Get to know us, come close to us, you will find how peaceful this community is."
